about.title: Downey Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Six people died in traffic collisions in Downey during 2025, according to public records, out of 829 injury crashes. Each of those numbers stands for a family in Los Angeles County that is now planning a funeral instead of a future. A wrongful death claim exists for exactly that situation: when someone's carelessness — on Lakewood Boulevard, Firestone Boulevard, Florence Avenue, Paramount Boulevard, or anywhere else — ends a life that should have continued. Under California law, a surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children have the first right to bring the claim; certain dependents and heirs may follow if none exist. The case is civil, separate from anything the district attorney decides to do. Recoverable losses reach beyond burial costs to the income your loved one would have provided and the companionship and guidance that cannot be replaced. The clock matters: two years from the date of death, and considerably less when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Downey families with an independent attorney, free of charge, who handles these claims on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Downey Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you're connected with can sort out where your family fits before any paperwork begins.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window shrinks sharply if a city, county, or state agency shares fault. Getting connected promptly protects that timeline.

items.title: Every loss accounted for
items.desc: Funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance are all recognized by California law. An independent attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on Firestone Boulevard. Does it matter that the driver hasn't been charged?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action, and it proceeds independently of whatever the district attorney chooses to do. Criminal charges can be helpful evidence, but their absence does not close the door on your family's claim. The standard of proof in a civil case is also different and generally lower.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring the claim?
items.answer: California gives the first right to a surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children. If there are none, certain financially dependent relatives and heirs may be able to step in. Because these rules can get complicated with blended families, it helps to have an attorney review your specific situation.

items.question: How long do we have to act in Downey?
items.answer: The general deadline is two years from the date of death. If a public entity — such as a city or county road agency — may be partly responsible, a formal claim often must be filed within a matter of months. Reaching out early gives the attorney time to preserve evidence and meet the shorter deadline if it applies.
